basis: Elemental iron (21 samples; the curator details say alpha-Fe) plus low-alloy steels quoted by grade (S355MC, C45). The measured window runs to 2194 K, so it crosses alpha->gamma at 1185 K and gamma->delta at 1667 K; the taxonomy has no separate prototype for fcc iron, so both are recorded as solid_solution_alloy with their own space groups.

basis: SnS1-xSex across the full x = 0.1-0.9 range. Both end members are the orthorhombic GeS-type Pnma layered structure, so the prototype holds along the whole axis even though the parent compound does not -- this is a solid solution, not a doped parent. The Pnma->Cmcm transition sits inside the measured 301-917 K window but its temperature moves with x (about 800 K at SnSe, 880 K at SnS), so the single value recorded here cannot cover the host. MP offers only computed Sn-Se-S orderings with no ICSD backing.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se), median 0.50 over 17 compositions. The Pnma->Cmcm transition temperature rises from ~800 K at SnSe to ~880 K at SnS, so the parent and the transition both depend on the composition.

Halogen donor on the anion site; the n-type route in the polycrystalline SnSe1-xSx papers.

dopant_roles.basis: The (Fe1-xVx)3Al series the first paper is titled for.

basis: Every composition is NdFeAsO0.89F0.11 with Ru or Rh on the Fe site -- the ZrCuSiAs-type 1111 oxypnictide, P4/nmm, MP mp-622621 with 9 ICSD references. At x = 0.11 the tetragonal-to-orthorhombic spin-density-wave distortion is already suppressed, so the 11-300 K window does not cross a structural transition.

dopant_roles.basis: F-for-O in the NdO layer is the electron-doping variable of the 1111 family, not an impurity.
Isovalent 4d-for-3d substitution; the paper studies its effect on the transport and Tc.

basis: BaSnO3 (11) and La-doped Ba1-xLaxSnO3 are the cubic Pm-3m perovskite, TEDesignLab mp-3163 with 11 ICSD references -- reference and composition agree. Ba2SnO4, the n=1 Ruddlesden-Popper member, appears in the reference but not among the compositions.

dopant_roles.basis: The n-type donor in 18 of the compositions.
BaSn1-xCoxO3 -- the p-type route in the third paper.
Ba1-xSrxSnO3 tunes the tolerance factor, not the carrier count.

basis: Every composition is Cu1.7Bi4.7Se8 with Zn or In substituted on one site or the other. Two of the three papers call it a pavonite homologue -- a module-built bismuth chalcogenide with a large low-symmetry cell, assembled from NaCl-type and Bi2Te3-type slabs -- rather than a tetradymite. MP offers only Cu6BiSe6 Pnma and CuBiSe2 R-3m, neither of which is the measured composition, so the structure has to be resolved per composition in stage 2.

Halogen donor on the anion site.

basis: CrN (17 of 34) in the rocksalt Fm-3m structure, MP mp-1000440 with 14 ICSD references; V, Mo and W substitute Cr and CrO0.09N0.91 puts O on the N site. dopant_roles.basis: Cr1-xVxN -- the hole-doping route in the second paper.
The heavy-element doping the third paper is titled for.
CrO0.09N0.91 -- deliberate anion-site oxygen, not milling residue; it is the subject of its paper.

basis: FeGa3 (7) with Co, Ge, Zn, Al and In substituted on one site or the other -- the tetragonal narrow-gap intermetallic, MP Ga3Fe P4_2/mnm mp-636368 with 6 ICSD references, and the third paper is titled for FeGa3-type compounds. One disagreement recorded rather than absorbed: the taxonomy lists fega3 at P-42m/P4n2, while both the reference and the structure literature give P4_2/mnm (136); the taxonomy entry looks wrong and should be corrected in v4.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe0.95Co0.05Ga3 -- electron doping on the transition-metal site.
FeGa2.85Ge0.15 -- donor on the main-group site.

basis: BaPb1-xBixO3 for x = 0.3-0.45 plus Sr-substituted variants -- the BaPbO3-BaBiO3 perovskite solid solution, orthorhombic through this composition range rather than ideal cubic, and the Bi breathing distortion grows as x rises. MP lists only ordered Ba-Bi-Pb-O supercells, two of them flagged AMBIGUOUS, and none is a measured composition, so no space group is asserted here.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.8Sr0.2 -- A-site size tuning, the subject of the first paper.
(Ba0.82K0.18)(Bi0.53Pb0.47)O3 -- the hole-doping variable in the third paper.

basis: YBaCo4O7 (6) with Zn, Al or Ga on the Co site is the swedenborgite of corner-sharing CoO4 tetrahedra, matching MP's BaYCo4O7 mp-1194048 (5 ICSD references). That entry gives Cmc2_1 (36) rather than the taxonomy's P6_3mc (186), and both are right: the compound is orthorhombic at room temperature and converts to hexagonal near 310 K, inside the measured window, so the two are recorded as successive phases of the same prototype. YBaCo2O5 is not a swedenborgite at all -- it is the oxygen-ordered 112 layered double perovskite and needs its own label.

dopant_roles.basis: YBaCo3.7Zn0.3O7 -- tetrahedral-site substitution stabilising the framework.

basis: Every composition carries a Ce guest -- CeFe3CoSb12, Ce0.9CoFe3Sb12, Ce0.9Fe3CoSb12 -- so the seed's skutterudite/filled_skutterudite pair collapses to filled_skutterudite alone; there is no unfilled composition here to split off. Ce at 1 of 17 atoms sits just above the 5 at.% cut, which is why it reads as a host element rather than as a filler in the dopant list. The composites add FeSb2 and BaFe12O19 as deliberate second phases, not as a second host structure. No reference line is offered for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: From the BaFe12O19 nanoinclusion and the Al2O3 film substrates, not from the lattice.
(BaFe12O19)0.001CeFe3CoSb12 -- a hexaferrite nanoinclusion added for phonon scattering, not a second cage filler.

basis: Cu4Mn2Te4 (7) with Cu/Mn off-stoichiometry and In, Zn, Fe, Co or Ni substitution is the whole host, and two of the four papers call it a ternary spinel or spinel-related. The reference is recorded as a partial disagreement: MP's only entry, Mn(CuTe)2 F-43m mp-1222078, is a cation-ordered derivative of the spinel framework rather than the Fd-3m aristotype the prototype names, and it carries no ICSD backing. The exact ordering has to be resolved in stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: Halogen donor on the anion site.

basis: HfNiSn (20 of 33) is the F-43m half-Heusler, MP mp-924128 at hull 0.000; Sb-for-Sn is the standard n-type donor and Zr and Ti substitute Hf isoelectronically. MP also lists the full Heusler HfNi2Sn mp-4828 with more ICSD references, but that is the usual interstitial-Ni second phase in these samples rather than a separate host structure -- worth resolving in stage 2 given the film samples present.

dopant_roles.basis: HfNiSn0.98Sb0.02 -- the standard n-type donor of the MNiSn half-Heuslers.
Hf1-xZrxNiSn -- mass-contrast alloying on the M site, not doping.
HfNiSn0.99In0.01 -- acceptor on the main-group site.

basis: BaCo0.4Fe0.4Zr0.1Y0.1O3 and its Y- and Zn-variants (13 of 32 samples) are the cubic mixed ionic-electronic conducting perovskite -- BCFZY, a solid-oxide-cell air electrode, which is why oxygen non-stoichiometry dominates its papers. The rest, Ba2Co2Fe12-2x(Ti,Mn)xO22, are Y-type hexaferrites: a block-stacked structure of spinel and Ba-containing layers with no taxonomy entry, proposed here as hexaferrite. The two cannot share a label and must be split on the Fe:Ba ratio. No reference line is offered for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: B-site in BCFZY, alongside Zr; stabilises the cubic perovskite and carries the proton conduction.
The (Ti-Mn) pair substitution of the hexaferrite series.

basis: All five compositions are Bi2YO4Cu2Se2 with I substituted for Se. It shares the anti-fluorite Cu2Se2 layer of BiCuSeO, which is why the 1111 seed is close, but this is recorded as a disagreement rather than a match: the oxide block is a thicker Bi2YO4 fluorite slab, the compound is body-centred I4/mmm rather than the P4/nmm ZrCuSiAs aristotype, and the papers describe it as a quasi-two-dimensional metal and a metallic derivative of BiOCuSe rather than a 1111 semiconductor. It may deserve its own prototype in v4. Neither reference line covers the formula.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi2YO4Cu2Se2-xIx -- the doping variable of the whole host, running to x = 0.2.

basis: Sm0.55Sr0.45MnO3 accounts for 25 of the 32 samples and the rest sit at x = 0.44-0.50 -- the half-doped orthorhombic manganite perovskite studied here for phase separation and giant magnetothermopower. MP's SrSm3Mn4O12 and SrSmMn2O6 are ordered supercells of the same perovskite framework at other Sr:Sm ratios, so they corroborate the framework without matching a composition.

dopant_roles.basis: Sm0.45Ce0.1Sr0.45MnO3 -- A-site electron doping against the Sr holes.

basis: (La1-yPry)0.625Ca0.375MnO3 -- the canonical phase-separated manganite. LaPrCaMn3O9 is the same compound written per three formula units. La and Pr share the A site across y = 0.40-0.60 with Ca held near 0.375, so the variable is the average A-site radius, not a dopant level, and no single parent compound applies. No reference line is offered for this chemistry.

solid_solution_axis.note: La/(La+Pr), median 0.52 over 6 compositions. Both are trivalent, so this tunes the A-site radius and the bandwidth rather than the carrier count; Ca sets the hole doping and stays near 0.375 throughout.

basis: (Ca,Sr)MnO3 across the full A-site range, with Ho on the A site and Mo on the Mn site as the actual donors. CaMnO3 is the orthorhombic Pnma perovskite and Sr substitution pushes it toward cubic, so the prototype holds along the axis while the space group does not. MP's entries are ordered Ca-Sr-Mn-O supercells carrying Fe, Ti or Nd and none is a measured composition.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ca/(Ca+Sr), median 0.56 over 15 compositions. Both divalent, so this is A-site size tuning; the doping comes from Ho on the A site and Mo on the Mn site.

dopant_roles.basis: Trivalent rare earth on the A site -- the electron donor in Ca0.45Sr0.4Ho0.15MnO3.
Ca0.7Sr0.3Mn0.96Mo0.04O3 -- B-site donor, the subject of the first paper.

basis: YbCd2Sb2 (14) with Mn, Zn, Mg or Ca substituted is the CaAl2Si2-type P-3m1 Zintl phase, MP mp-9257 at hull 0.000 -- the 1-2-2 stoichiometry, the trigonal reference and the papers (which all say Zintl phase YbCd2-xMxSb2) agree.

dopant_roles.basis: Monovalent acceptor on the cation site -- the standard carrier control in 1-2-2 Zintls.
YbCd2-xZnxSb2 -- isovalent alloying on the anion framework site.

basis: CoSb3-xTex for x = 0.2-0.3 (CoSb2.8Te0.2 and neighbours) is binary CoSb3 skutterudite with Te donors on the Sb ring -- unfilled, so the binary prototype rather than the filled one. The reference is recorded as absent rather than supporting: the two MP entries offered, Co2SbTe and CoSbTe, sit at hull 0.396 and 0.471 with no ICSD backing and are not this compound. Co0.98Ni0.02(Sb0.25Te0.75)3 is far too Te-rich for the skutterudite field and should be checked separately.

dopant_roles.basis: CoSb2.75Ge0.05Te0.2 -- Ge and Te are co-substituted on the pnictogen ring.
Co1-xNix -- electron doping on the transition-metal site.

basis: Pr1-xAxMnO3 manganites with A = Sr, Ca, Na, K or Te: PrMnO3 Pnma mp-25037 (9 ICSD references) is the parent and every composition is an A-site-substituted version of it. Reference and composition agree here, which is not the case for most of the manganite hosts in this chunk.

dopant_roles.basis: Pr1-xSrxMnO3 -- the hole-doping variable in 17 compositions.
Pr0.9Te0.1MnO3 -- an unusual A-site substituent; worth confirming against the paper.

basis: PbPdO2 (9) with Li, Cu or Co on the Pd site is the entire host. It is a layered oxide built from square-planar PdO4 units, MP PdPbO2 Imma mp-22367 with 4 ICSD references at hull 0.000, and it matches no existing prototype -- not a delafossite (no triangular two-coordinate Pd net), not a perovskite, not tenorite. Proposed as pbpdo2_layered in prototypes_proposed.jsonl before use; the verification gate checks prototype_id against seed v3 only, so this record needs the proposal folded in.

dopant_roles.basis: PbPd1-xLixO2 -- the hole-doping variable, named in the curator detail and its paper title.
The third paper is about Cu doping of PbPdO2.

basis: RuO2 is the only composition (all 31 samples) and is rutile P4_2/mnm, MP mp-825 at hull 0.000 with 16 ICSD references -- the cleanest agreement in this chunk. The other two MP entries are not thermal phases: Pa-3 is the pyrite-type high-pressure polymorph and Fm-3m a cubic high-pressure form, so both go in other_polymorphs.

other_polymorphs.note: Pa-3 pyrite-type RuO2, 5 ICSD references at hull 0.066; formed under pressure, not reached by heating at ambient pressure.
Cubic RuO2 at hull 0.193 with 3 ICSD references; a high-pressure form, not a thermal phase.

basis: AgSnmSbTem+2 (AgSn4SbTe6, AgSn2SbTe4, AgSn5SbTe7) and the (AgSbTe2)1-x(SnTe)x pseudobinaries: a rocksalt matrix with Ag, Sb and Sn sharing the cation site -- the Sn analogue of TAGS and LAST, and the first paper is titled for exactly that series. Neither reference line covers the quaternary, so no mp_id is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Halogen donor on the anion site.
The curator records AgSn4SbTe6(SiC)0.03 -- SiC is a dispersed second phase, not a substituent.

basis: Ca5Al2Sb6 (5) with Na, Zn, Mn or In substituted is the Pbam 5-2-6 Zintl chain compound, TEDesignLab Ca5(AlSb3)2 mp-8439 at hull 0.000 -- reference, stoichiometry and paper titles all agree. Ca3AlSb3 (2 samples) is the Pnma 3-1-3 Zintl, a different prototype; the reference names it too, at space group 62, without an mp_id.

dopant_roles.basis: Ca5Al1.9Zn0.1Sb6 -- acceptor on the polyanion site.
Ca4.75Na0.25Al2Sb6 -- the main carrier-concentration knob in this family.
The third paper is titled for Mn-doped Ca5Al2Sb6.

basis: (Y,Pr,Nd,Sm)Ba2Cu3O7 is about 15 of the 30 samples -- YBCO with rare earths sharing the Y site. Y and Pr appear as dopant candidates only because that site is shared three or four ways, not because they are dilute. (Ba2CuO3)10(CaCuO2)3 is a different structure, an infinite-layer/chain intergrowth, and must be split off. MP's Ba-Cu-O binaries (Ba2CuO3, BaCuO2) are the flux and precursor phases, not the measured compounds. YBCO's orthorhombic-to-tetragonal oxygen-ordering transition near 950 K falls inside the measured 11-1179 K window and is recorded as two phases of the same prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: A host constituent of YBa2Cu3O7 pushed below the 5 at.% cut by sharing its site with Pr or Nd -- not a dopant.
Y1-xPrxBa2Cu3O7 -- Pr suppresses superconductivity; x is the variable of most of these papers.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [47, 123], ICSD-backed references for this host report [65, 10, 14, 71]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: Ba1-xEuxTiO3 for x = 0.3-0.7 with Nb on the Ti site -- the ABO3 perovskite throughout. Both end members are perovskites (BaTiO3 tetragonal at room temperature, EuTiO3 cubic), so the prototype holds across the series even though the symmetry does not; no space group is asserted for that reason. BaTiO3's ferroelectric tetragonal-to-cubic transition near 390 K lies inside the measured window, but 30-70% Eu shifts and suppresses it, so no single transition temperature covers this host and none is recorded. No reference line is offered for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.7Eu0.3Ti1-xNbxO3 -- the B-site donor, the subject of the first paper.

basis: Cu2CdSnSe4 (10) with In, Zn or Mn substituted and Cu-rich off-stoichiometry: the I-42m stannite quaternary diamond-like, TEDesignLab CdCu2SnSe4 mp-16565 at hull 0.000. Reference and composition agree.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu2CdSn1-xInxSe4 -- the deliberate carrier-tuning substitution here.
Cu2Cd1-xMnxSnSe4, named in the curator detail.
Cu2.05Cd0.95SnSe4 -- Cu-rich/Cd-poor off-stoichiometry sets the hole count, as in CZTS.

basis: Two different Fe:(Sb+Te) ratios sit in this host and they are different structures. FeSb2Te, FeSb2.2Te0.8, FeSb2.05Te0.95 and FeSb2.15Te0.85 are all M:X = 1:3 -- unfilled ternary skutterudites, which is what the lead paper calls them. FeSb1.84Te0.16 (6 samples) is M:X = 1:2, Te-doped marcasite FeSb2, and the other two papers are about doped FeSb2 crystals. MP's FeSbTe entries sit at hull 0.40-0.55 and describe neither, so the split has to be made on the ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: The curator records FeSb2.2Te0.8 with 1-10 mol% InSb added, so In is a second phase rather than a substituent.

basis: 20 of the 30 samples are equimolar five-A-site manganites -- Nd0.2Ca0.2Sr0.2Ba0.2Y0.2MnO3 and its La, Ho and Lu analogues -- where every A cation sits at 4 at.% and falls below the split, which is the only reason this host reads as Mn-O at all. They are perovskites with a configurationally disordered A site. The rest are binaries: MnO2 (rutile-type pyrolusite, mp-19326), MnO (rocksalt, mp-19006, 14 ICSD references) and Mn3O4 hausmannite (spinel, mp-18759). One taxonomy disagreement recorded rather than followed: the high_entropy_alloy entry claims the five-A-site manganites in this host, which would file an oxide perovskite in an alloy class -- the structure is a perovskite and the disorder is a property of one sublattice.

dopant_roles.basis: A-site constituent of an equimolar high-entropy manganite at 4 at.%, not a dilute dopant.
A-site constituent of the equimolar manganite.

basis: PbTe with Ag2Te: (PbTe)0.945(Ag2Te)0.055 and Pb42.32Te44.12Ag13.55 are LAST-type nanostructured rocksalt PbTe, and La and Na are the donor and acceptor on the Pb site. The matrix is rocksalt; the Ag2Te nanoprecipitates the first paper is titled for are a second phase within each sample, not a second host structure, so this is not split per composition. No reference line is offered for this chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb1-xLaxTe -- the donor in the La/Ag cosubstitution paper.
The standard p-type acceptor in PbTe.

basis: Al74.6Re17.4Si8 and the rest of the Al82.6-xRe17.4Six series (x = 7-11) are the 1/1 cubic approximant the second paper is titled for, matching MP's Al17(Re2Si)2 Pm-3 mp-16569 at hull 0.000. One composition does not belong: Al5.7Re4.7Si4.3 is Al6Re5Si4, which its paper calls a MoSi2-type narrow-band-gap intermetallic -- a C11b structure with no taxonomy entry -- so it is parked as unresolved_crystalline rather than folded into the approximant. The curator notes the Al71.6-x formula in the paper totals 89 atoms, so the reported fractions were renormalised.

La1-xCaxFeO3 for x = 0.3-0.7 with Co, Ni or Cr on the Fe site -- the orthorhombic GdFeO3-type perovskite, corroborated by MP's CaLa2(FeO3)3 Pnma mp-1227525 at hull 0.000. One thing to carry into stage 2: at high Ca content and strong reduction this system orders its oxygen vacancies into the brownmillerite Ca2Fe2O5 structure, and several of these papers are about oxygen non-stoichiometry in air electrodes, so some samples may not be cubic-derived perovskites at measurement temperature.

Every composition is Yb-filled (YbFe4Sb12, Yb0.9-0.95FexM0.5Sb12), so the seed's skutterudite/filled_skutterudite pair resolves to filled_skutterudite alone -- there is no unfilled composition in this host. MP's Yb(FeSb3)4 Im-3 mp-1207658 at hull 0.000 is the same phase. The Yb fraction y is the filling level that sets the carrier count, not a dopant level, and belongs to stage 3 as such.

dopant_roles.basis: YbFe3.5Ni0.5Sb12 -- electron doping on the framework transition-metal site.
If real, a co-filler in the icosahedral void rather than a framework substituent; worth confirming.
Double filling with Yb -- the Cey/2Yby/2Fe4-xCoxSb12 paper.

basis: Mg2Ge (15 of 29) with Sb and Bi donors on the Ge site is the cubic antifluorite Fm-3m, MP mp-408 at hull 0.000 with 8 ICSD references. Mg2.2Ge is Mg excess on the same lattice, not a different phase. Reference and composition agree.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg2Ge0.98Sb0.02 -- the standard n-type donor of the Mg2X antifluorites.

basis: Ge1-xPbxSe0.5Te0.5 for x = 0.1-0.5, with both sublattices alloyed at once. GeTe is rhombohedral R3m while PbTe and PbSe are rocksalt, and roughly 20% Pb removes the rhombohedral distortion at room temperature, so the Ge-rich compositions are rhombohedral and the Pb-rich ones are already cubic -- the host must be split per composition. Recorded at the low-temperature end as gete_rhombohedral with rocksalt as the alternative. The R3m->Fm-3m transition falls inside the measured 200-800 K window for the Ge-rich compositions, but its temperature drops steeply with Pb and Se content, so the value here cannot cover the host. MP offers only GeTe(PbSe)2 P3m1 at hull 0.027 with no ICSD backing.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te), median 0.50 over 28 compositions. Ge and Pb alloy on the cation site over the same range, and it is the Pb fraction that decides whether a composition is rhombohedral or cubic.

dopant_roles.basis: Cu is often interstitial rather than substitutional in GeTe-based alloys; confirm against the paper.

basis: LaSrNiO4 and La1.5Sr0.5NiO4 are the n=1 K2NiF4 member of the (La,Sr)n+1NinO3n+1 series -- one NiO2 layer per rocksalt block -- and the 1:1:1:4 stoichiometry admits no other reading. The O3.97/O4.00 variants are oxygen non-stoichiometry on the same lattice. MP's ICSD-ranked primaries for this host are computed multi-cation cells (Sr4La4Cr(NiO5)3 P2/m, Sr5La5Cu(NiO5)4 P1) that are not this compound; its SrLaNiO4 Cmcm (63) mp-1218178 at hull 0.001 is the relevant entry, and Cmcm is an orthorhombic distortion of the I4/mmm aristotype rather than a different prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: LaSrNi1-xScxO4 -- Sc3+ on the octahedral Ni site, the solid solution the paper is built around.
B-site substitution by analogy with Fe.

basis: LaRhO3 with B-site substitution (LaRh1-xNixO3, LaCo1-xRhxO3) is an ABO3 perovskite, GdFeO3-tilted rather than cubic: MP gives LaRhO3 Pnma (62) mp-5163 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, the only entry for the host, and it agrees with the composition.

dopant_roles.basis: LaRh1-xNixO3 -- acceptor on the octahedral B site; x runs to 0.2 in this host.
LaCo1-xRhxO3 is a full solid solution; the compositions below 5 at.% are its dilute end.
A-site acceptor, the usual hole-doping knob for LaBO3.
Divalent acceptor on the B site; could also sit on the A site -- needs the paper.

basis: Ni4Sb8.2Sn3.8 is Ni4(Sb,Sn)12 -- the CoSb3 skutterudite framework with Sn sharing the pnictogen rings to balance the electron count for Ni, and both papers call these skutterudites. Ba0.42Ni4Sb8.2Sn3.8, Eu0.8Ni4Sb5.8Sn6.2 and the Yb variant put a guest in the icosahedral void, so the host holds both the unfilled and the filled framework and must be split per composition. MP has no Im-3 entry for the host; its Ni4(SnSb3)3 Cm (8) mp-1220099 at hull 0.005 is a computed Sb/Sn-ordered decoration of the same 4:12 framework with no ICSD backing, and Ni6SnSb Pmm2 is a different compound entirely.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.42Ni4Sb8.2Sn3.8 -- guest in the icosahedral void; the filling fraction sets the carrier count and belongs to stage 3 as a filling level, not a dopant level.
Same void as Ba and Eu.

basis: Every composition is SrxPryTiO3 with x+y < 1 -- A-site-deficient SrTiO3 with Pr3+ donors, the standard n-type titanate route (the papers are 'praseodymium in strontium titanate' and 'A-site cation deficiency'). The TiO3 framework fixes the corner-sharing octahedral net; the A-site vacancies are the carrier and phonon-scattering knob, not a second phase. No TEDesignLab or Materials Project entry exists for this host, so this rests on composition and materials knowledge alone.

Fe80B20, Fe85B15 and Fe83B14Si1.5C1.5 sit on the Fe-B glass-forming eutectic and 20 of 21 samples with a recorded form are melt-spun Ribbon, so the seed's metallic_glass holds for the bulk of the host -- but not for all of it: FeB and Fe2B are crystalline line compounds from the 'Seebeck coefficients of iron group elements borides' paper. FeB is the B27/FeB chain type (MP Pnma (62) mp-20787, 12 ICSD refs) and Fe2B is the CuAl2 C16 type (MP I4/mcm (140) mp-1915, 12 ICSD refs), so the host needs three prototypes and a per-composition split. Note the measured range reaches 962 K, above the ~700 K crystallisation of Fe-B glasses, so the ribbons may not stay amorphous to the top of their own curves.

dopant_roles.basis: (Fe0.98Ni0.02)84B16 -- the paper's small Co/Ni additions to the glass former.
Same paper; Co and Ni are added on the metal sublattice of the glass.
Fe83B14Si1.5C1.5 -- Si is a glass-forming metalloid component of the ribbon, not a dilute dopant.
As Si: a metalloid glass-forming addition, not milling residue here.
Transition-metal additions on the metal sublattice; in a glass there is no crystallographic site, so 'substitutional' means the metal sublattice of the amorphous network.

basis: Ba8Ni3.5Ge42.1, Ba8Ni4Ge42, Ba8Ni5Ge41 and the Zn-bearing variants are all Ba8E46 -- eight guests per 46-atom framework, the type-I clathrate stoichiometry, and every paper says clathrate. MP's Ba4Ni3Ge20 Pm-3n (223) mp-30169 is the same structure written on a half cell (Ba8Ni6Ge40) and carries the type-I space group with 1 ICSD reference; the other entry, Ba2Ni5Ge4 C2/m, is an unrelated intermetallic.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba8Ni2.9Zn1.2Ge41.9 -- Zn replaces Ge in the covalent cage framework alongside Ni and sets the electron count; it is a framework variable, not a dopant on a guest site.

basis: BaPbO3 and BaPb1-xBixO3 are ABO3 perovskites and the papers name them as such. The references show the octahedral-tilt family rather than one structure: TEDesignLab gives BaPbO3 C2/m (12) mp-20461 with 14 ICSD refs as primary, Imma (74) mp-22230 with 11, I4/mcm (140) mp-20991 with 2, and MP adds cubic Pm-3m mp-21280 with 5. These are tilt variants of one prototype, not different prototypes, and the cubic aristotype is the least attested of them. BaPbO3 is reported to untilt towards tetragonal and then cubic on heating inside the measured 11-1172 K window, but the prototype does not change and no transition temperature can be given without the paper, so none is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: BaPb1-xBixO3 is a full solid solution; the compositions here are its dilute end on the B site, and Bi is what drives the metal-insulator crossover.
Ba0.8Sr0.2Pb0.85Bi0.15O3 -- isovalent A-site substitution that tunes the tilt angle.
BaPb1-xZrxO3, the subject of one of the papers.
A-site donor in the Sr- and La-substituted series.

basis: Cr2Se3 and Cr1.96Se3 are the vacancy-ordered NiAs derivative -- one third of the metal layers empty, which is what makes the R-3 cell (TEDesignLab Cr2Se3 R-3 (148) mp-1079651, hull 0.000, 4 ICSD refs) rather than a separate prototype from CrSe P6_3/mmc (194, 6 refs). The seed's nias therefore holds for the Cr2-xSe3 compositions. It does not hold for BaxCr5Se8 (x = 0.50-0.55), which the paper calls a ternary pseudo-hollandite: Ba sits in tunnels of a Cr5Se8 framework, so that group needs hollandite and the host must be split per composition. Recording it under hollandite is itself a stretch -- the taxonomy defines hollandite as an AxM8O16 framework oxide and this is the selenide analogue; flagged for review.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba0.5Cr5Se8 -- a tunnel cation in the pseudo-hollandite framework, structurally a guest rather than a substituent. The role vocabulary has no tunnel-cation value; cage_filler is the closest.
The chromium sulfo-selenide paper: S and Se share the anion site over the whole range.
Cr1-xMnxSe-type substitution on the metal site; the p-n control paper uses it.

basis: RuIn3 dominates the host and the papers state the FeGa3 type outright ('FeGa3-type narrow-bandgap intermetallic compounds'). MP's In3Ru P4_2/mnm (136) mp-607450 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references is that structure. Worth flagging: the taxonomy gives fega3 a typical space group of 'P-42m (111) / P4n2', which does not match the FeGa3/RuIn3 aristotype P4_2/mnm (136) that both ICSD-backed entries here report -- the taxonomy entry, not the assignment, looks wrong. Ru0.25In0.75 is Ru1-yIn3 with metal vacancies, the third of the three series the papers study (Sn-substituted, Zn-substituted, Ru-deficient), not a different compound.

other_polymorphs.note: In3Ru P-4n2, hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference: a lower-symmetry ordering of the same framework rather than a phase reached by heating.

dopant_roles.basis: RuIn3-xZnx -- acceptor on the In site, one of the two doping series in the papers.
RuIn3-xSnx -- donor on the In site.

basis: Every composition is Zr3Ni3Sb4 with small substitutions on the Ni site, which is the Y3Au3Sb4 3-3-4 type; MP's Zr3Ni3Sb4 I-43d (220) mp-17926 at hull 0.000 confirms both stoichiometry and space group. The host's other MP entries (Zr3NiSb7 Pnma with 4 ICSD refs, ZrNi2Sb P6_3/mmc with 3) are different Zr-Ni-Sb line compounds and no composition here matches them -- an ICSD-count ranking picks the wrong phase for this host.

dopant_roles.basis: Zr3Ni3-xCoxSb4 -- acceptor on the Ni site, the main series in the papers.
Zr3Ni3-xCuxSb4 -- donor on the same site.

basis: AgBiSe2 is a rocksalt-derived ternary, as the seed says, but not the disordered cubic one at the temperatures most of these curves start from: at room temperature Ag and Bi order into alternating (111) layers, giving the rhombohedral R-3m structure that MP lists as AgBiSe2 R-3m (166) mp-27916, hull 0.002, 4 ICSD refs and the only ICSD-backed entry for the host. That ordered rocksalt superstructure is the alpha-NaFeO2 type, so the low-temperature end is recorded there and cation-disordered rocksalt is the high-temperature phase. The ordering is the point of these papers -- the reversible p-n-p switching is driven by the transitions -- so the host genuinely spans them inside its 36-810 K window. The seed's rocksalt is kept as the alternative because the cubic phase is real, just not the ambient one.

other_polymorphs.note: AgBiSe2 I4_1/amd at hull 0.043 and P4/mmm mp-1229087 at hull 0.104 are computed cation orderings with no ICSD backing; neither is reached on heating.

dopant_roles.basis: AgBi0.975Pb0.025Se2 -- aliovalent acceptor on the Bi site, one of the alio-valent dopants the title names.
AgBiSe1.98Cl0.02 -- halogen donor on the anion site.
Only two compositions; the site is a guess from the cation radius.

basis: CuAgSe carries 15 of the 27 samples and the rest are its off-stoichiometric variants, so this is the ordered ternary member of the Cu2Se/Ag2Se superionic family rather than a Cu2Se-Ag2Se alloy -- the solid-solution axis reports a median Ag/(Ag+Cu) of exactly 0.50 because the compound is 1:1:1, not because the host is an alloy series, and that is recorded in the axis note rather than as a parent compound. The low-temperature phase is the ordered tetragonal one (MP CuAgSe P4/nmm (129) mp-1225840, hull 0.052, the only entry and not ICSD-backed), and it converts to the cubic superionic phase with liquid-like Cu/Ag inside the measured 18-775 K window. The taxonomy's default for that transition is ~400 K, which is the Cu2Se value; for CuAgSe it is nearer 470 K, so the phase record uses 470 K and this is a deliberate departure from the taxonomy default.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ag/(Ag+Cu) over 13 compositions with median 0.50. This is not a genuine alloy axis: almost every composition is the stoichiometric ternary CuAgSe, and the spread comes from Cu- or Ag-deficient variants (Cu0.99AgSe, CuAg0.99Se) plus one Cu2Se-rich outlier (Cu1.98Ag0.2Se).

dopant_roles.basis: Te-doped ternary CuAgSe -- same-valence anion substitution, the subject of one paper.
Cation site of a structure whose cations are mobile above the transition, so the site is only meaningful in the ordered phase.

basis: SmBa2Cu3O7-delta is the 123 structure with Sm on the Y site; MP's Ba2SmCu3O7 Pmmm (47) mp-21451 carries 19 ICSD references, by far the best-attested entry for the host, and matches the compositions directly. The O6.835-O7 spread is the oxygen doping variable of the CuO chain layer, not an impurity or a second phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Fe and Mn enter the CuO chain site in RBa2Cu3O7, which is how the percolation paper suppresses the thermopower.
SmBa2-xSrxCu3O7-delta, the subject of one paper -- isovalent A-site substitution.
Three compositions carry H; most likely moisture or a hydrogenation treatment rather than a lattice species. Needs the paper.

basis: Tl9BiTe6 and its Bi-deficient variants (Tl9Bi0.96-1.01Te6) are the Tl5Te3 type with Bi ordered on one Tl site -- MP's Tl9BiTe6 I4/m (87) mp-34361 at hull 0.000 is that ordered variant of I4/mcm. TlBiTe2 is not: it is the rhombohedral ordered rocksalt (MP TlBiTe2 R-3m (166) mp-27438, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD refs), exactly the split the taxonomy's own discriminate_from anticipates, so the host carries both prototypes and must be divided by stoichiometry. Note the agreement check will read a disagreement here: the only ICSD-backed space group for this host is 166 from TlBiTe2, while the dominant composition is the 87/140 Tl5Te3 phase.

dopant_roles.basis: Tl9Bi1-xSnxTe6 -- acceptor on the ordered Bi site; the 'variants of Tl9SbTe6 and Tl9BiTe6' paper is built on it.

reference_disagreement: assigned sg [87], ICSD-backed references for this host report [166]. Confidence downgraded by verify_assignments.py; a disagreement can still be correct where the reference describes the chemistry rather than the sample.

basis: CaZn2Sb2 is the largest composition and is the 1-2-2 CaAl2Si2-type layered Zintl (MP Ca(ZnSb)2 P-3m1 (164) mp-7429, hull 0.000, 1 ICSD ref); Ca9Zn4.5-4.6Sb9 is the 9-4-9 Zintl with its partially occupied interstitial site (MP Ca9Zn4Sb9 Pbam (55) mp-21594, hull 0.000). Both seed hypotheses are therefore correct for different compositions and the host splits cleanly on the Zn:Ca ratio, 2:1 against roughly 1:2.

dopant_roles.basis: Acceptor on the tetrahedral framework site of the Zn2Sb2 layer.
Eu0.01Ca0.99Zn2Sb2 and Eu0.2Ca0.8Zn2Sb2 -- EuZn2Sb2 is isostructural, so this is the dilute end of a full solid solution on the A site.

basis: Both seed hypotheses are real and the host has to be split on stoichiometry. Fe1-xCoxSi at x = 0.1-0.9 is the chiral cubic B20 monosilicide solid solution (two of the three papers -- 'transition-metal monosilicides' and the Fe1-xCoxSi quantum-phase-transition study), and Co2FeSi is the L21 full Heusler (MP FeCo2Si Fm-3m (225) mp-1065751, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD refs, the best-attested entry for the host). B20 is recorded as the primary because the monosilicide compositions outnumber the Heusler ones, but the two are comparable in sample count, so this is a split, not a majority. MP has no P2_13 entry for the ternary at all -- its FeCoSi Pnma mp-1102660 (1 ICSD ref, hull 0.064) is a TiNiSi-type ordering, not the B20 phase these papers make.

Co1-xNixSb3 (written variously as Co0.8Ni0.2Sb3, Co7.3Ni2.7Sb30 and the parse-mangled Co0.8Sb2.4Ni0.2Sb0.2, which sums to Co0.8Ni0.2Sb2.6) is the binary skutterudite framework with Ni donors on the Co site, and the papers say so. Ce0.3Ni1.5Co2.5Sb12 is filled, so the host also needs filled_skutterudite and splits on whether a filler is present. MP's Co4NiSb12 Im-3 (204) mp-1106327 has the right space group and 1 ICSD reference but sits at hull 0.159, which reflects how poorly the 2019 dump handles the mixed Co/Ni framework rather than instability of the phase. Three samples are films, where a metastable polymorph would be reachable, but nothing in the compositions suggests one.

dopant_roles.basis: Ce0.3Ni1.5Co2.5Sb12 -- guest in the icosahedral void, not a substituent; the filling fraction is a stage-3 filling level.
Co0.79Ni0.21Sb2.88Sn0.12 -- acceptor on the pnictogen ring, compensating the Ni donors.

basis: ZrCoSb1-xSnx is the canonical p-type half-Heusler: 18 valence electrons at x = 0, Sn on the Sb site as the acceptor, and every paper title says half-Heusler. Hf and Ti appear only as isovalent partners on the Zr site. Sn is above the 5 at.% split and so is counted as a host element here, but it is the doping variable of this system, which matters for stage 3. There is no TEDesignLab or Materials Project entry for this host, so nothing external tests the call; the cubic F-43m C1b structure is inferred from the 1:1:1 stoichiometry and the chemistry.

dopant_roles.basis: Zr1-xTixCoSb0.7Sn0.3 -- same-group substitution on the Zr site that scatters phonons without changing the electron count.
Hf0.15Zr0.85CoSb0.8Sn0.2; Hf and Zr are interchangeable on this site.

basis: YCrO3 with Ca on the Y site and Co/Ni/Mn on the Cr site is an orthorhombic GdFeO3-tilted perovskite; MP's YCrO3 Pnma (62) mp-18725 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references matches. The host's other ICSD-backed entry, YCrO4 I4_1/amd with 3 refs, is the zircon-type chromate -- a different oxidation state and structure, and no composition here has the 1:4 oxygen ratio, so the reference ranking would mislead if followed on count alone. Ca is present in 22 of the compositions at just under the 5 at.% cut, but it is 20% of the Y site and is the carrier knob of this system, not a trace impurity.

dopant_roles.basis: Y0.8Ca0.2CrO3 -- 20% of the A site, the acceptor that makes these chromites conduct; below 5 at.% of the formula only because oxygen dominates the denominator.
Y0.8Ca0.2Cr1-xCoxO3, the Ca- and Co-doped interconnect paper.
Y0.8Ca0.2Cr1-xNixO3 -- B-site substitution and its defect chemistry are one paper's whole subject.

basis: FeSe1-xTex across x = 0.1-0.9 is the '11' iron chalcogenide -- anti-PbO layers of edge-sharing FeCh4 tetrahedra, P4/nmm -- and Se and Te share the single anion site, so one prototype covers the whole axis. The MP entries for this host (Fe2TeSe P4mm, Fe3Te2Se P4mm, Fe4TeSe3 Amm2, all hull 0.01-0.08 with no ICSD backing) are computed Se/Te orderings of that same layer, not different structures; one is flagged AMBIGUOUS. FeSe itself undergoes a tetragonal-to-orthorhombic nematic distortion near 90 K, inside the measured 10-300 K window, but it is a symmetry-lowering distortion of this prototype rather than a new one, and Te substitution above x ~ 0.1 suppresses it, so it is noted rather than recorded as a phase. Fe1.01 and Fe1.14 are interstitial excess Fe, the well-known non-stoichiometry of this system.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) over 17 compositions, median 0.50. Both end members are the same anti-PbO structure, so the axis changes the lattice parameters and the electronic state but not the prototype.

basis: 17 of 27 samples are plain MoS2 and the rest are V- or Cu-doped MoS2, which is the 2H trigonal-prismatic dichalcogenide: MP MoS2 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-2815, hull 0.000, 12 ICSD refs. The references disagree with each other here and the MP one is right: TEDesignLab's only entry for this host is Mo2S3 P2_1/m (11) mp-1627 at hull 0.094, a different compound that no composition in the host matches, so the tier-1 preference for TEDesignLab has to be overridden. Mo3S4 (9 ICSD refs) is the Chevrel-type phase and is likewise absent from the compositions. One film sample could in principle be the metastable 1T polytype, but nothing in the data says so.

dopant_roles.basis: VxMoS2 for x = 0.01-0.1 -- acceptor on the metal site of the layer.

MoS2Cu0.065 -- Cu in a layered sulfide normally intercalates into the van der Waals gap rather than replacing Mo; the paper is on Cu-doped MoS2 nanosheets. Substitution on Mo is the alternative and needs the paper.

basis: TaN, TaN0.89 and TaN1.35 are the substoichiometric-to-overstoichiometric delta-TaN films that one paper names outright in its title ('the metal-to-insulator transition in rocksalt TaN'), and the taxonomy's own note already cites TaN0.89 as the wide-non-stoichiometry example. MP's TaN Fm-3m (225) mp-251 carries 13 ICSD references, the most of any entry for this host, although its hull of 0.327 reflects that the equilibrium bulk phase at exact 1:1 is the hexagonal one rather than the rocksalt -- the rocksalt is what sputtering makes and what ICSD therefore holds. Ta3N5 is a different structure entirely (MP Cmcm (63) mp-27488, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD refs), an orthorhombic pseudobrookite-related nitride with no taxonomy entry, so those two samples are parked in unresolved_crystalline rather than forced into the rocksalt label.

dopant_roles.basis: Ta0.932Si0.068N0.56 from the reactively sputtered Ta-Si-N films. Si may sit on the Ta site, but Ta-Si-N films are more often nanocomposites of TaN grains in an amorphous Si3N4 boundary phase; needs the paper.
One composition; Ag has no site in the rocksalt nitride.
Oxygen in a sputtered nitride is residual-gas contamination, not a lattice species.

basis: The Tl10-xLnxTe6 series (Ln = La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd) that dominates the compositions is the Tl5Te3 type with the rare earth ordered on one Tl site -- MP Tl5Te3 I4/mcm (140) mp-174, hull 0.005, 5 ICSD refs -- so the seed holds for most of the host. Two other structures are present and the host must be split. TlTe (MP I4/mcm (140) mp-2081, hull 0.000, 9 ICSD refs, the best-attested entry here) is the mixed-valence TlSe/B37 type, which shares the space group with Tl5Te3 but is a different structure. Tl2Te is monoclinic and is neither: the taxonomy's tl5te3 note lists 'Tl9BiTe6, Tl4SnTe3, Tl2Te' as members, and that third one looks wrong -- Tl2Te is a distinct C2/m phase, not Tl5Te3 written differently -- so it is parked in unresolved_crystalline and the taxonomy note is flagged. One paper measures liquid Tl-Te solutions and the 295-1066 K range runs above the melting point of these phases, so some curves describe a melt with no crystal prototype at all.

dopant_roles.basis: Tl9.75Gd0.25Te6 -- the rare earth takes the ordered Tl(1) site of Tl5Te3 and sets the carrier count; it is 2-7% of the formula but a large fraction of that one site.
Tl9BiTe6 chemistry -- Bi orders on the same site.

basis: Cu1-xAgxInTe2 over the whole 0.18-0.80 range is chalcopyrite: CuInTe2 and AgInTe2 are both I-42d ordered zincblende superstructures, so the Ag/Cu axis changes the tetragonal distortion -- which is exactly what the 'pseudocubic' paper tunes -- without changing the prototype. MP offers only computed Cu/Ag orderings of the same diamond-like net (In2CuAgTe4 I-4 (82) mp-1224246, In4Cu3AgTe8 P1, In4CuAg3Te8 P-4, hull 0.006-0.010, none ICSD-backed), which is a reasonable picture of a partially ordered quaternary but not independent evidence.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ag/(Ag+Cu) over 19 compositions, median 0.20. Both end members are chalcopyrite, so no parent compound has to be chosen for the structure; the axis matters for the lattice distortion and for stage 3, not for the prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: CuGaTe2 is isostructural, so Ga on the In site is same-valence alloying rather than doping.

basis: MgB2 and (MgB2)1.9Co0.1 account for 19 of 26 samples and are the AlB2 C32 type -- graphite-like B layers with Mg between them -- MP MgB2 P6/mmm (191) mp-763, hull 0.000, 29 ICSD references, the strongest attestation in this chunk. The seed is therefore right for the bulk of the host but not for all of it: Mg7.0B100, Mg7.5B99, Mg6.9B98 and Mg7.7B100 are Mg:B near 1:13-14, far past MgB4 and MgB7, and are boron-framework materials rather than the diboride. The taxonomy's boron_carbide entry explicitly covers beta-rhombohedral boron alongside B4C, so those four compositions are recorded there rather than as a new prototype, and the host splits on the B:Mg ratio.

dopant_roles.basis: (MgB2)1.9Co0.1 is written as an addition, and transition metals added to MgB2 usually form Co-B second phases rather than entering the lattice; the paper claims structural and electronic effects, so partial substitution on the Mg site is the alternative. Needs the paper.
C-for-B is the one well-established substitution in MgB2, on the boron honeycomb.
Ti additions to MgB2 are standard as a second-phase pinning or densification aid.

basis: Both seed hypotheses are present and the host splits on stoichiometry. Sr1-xLnxCuO2 (Ln = La, Nd, Eu) is the infinite-layer ACuO2 phase -- flat CuO2 sheets with no apical oxygen, electron-doped by the trivalent substitution -- and carries the most samples; Sr2CuO3 is the 1D chain cuprate (MP Immm (71) mp-5456, hull 0.000, 9 ICSD refs). The references describe the chemistry rather than these samples and must be read carefully here: MP's SrCuO2 entry is Cmcm (63) mp-5787 with 6 ICSD refs, which is the ambient zigzag-chain SrCuO2, not the infinite-layer polymorph. That polymorph is metastable at ambient pressure and is made under high pressure or as an epitaxial film, which is consistent with the 4 Film and 5 SingleCrystal samples here, so the space-group disagreement is expected rather than an error. One further composition, (In0.2Pb0.55Cu0.25)Sr2(Ca0.5Y0.5)Cu2O7, is neither: it is a Pb/In-1212 cuprate, structurally the 123 family with the CuO chain layer replaced, so ybco_cuprate is listed as a third alternative for that single sample.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr1-xLaxCuO2 -- trivalent on the divalent A site is the electron doping of the infinite-layer cuprate, the whole point of these papers.
Sr0.875Nd0.125CuO2, same site and role as La.
Monovalent on the A site would hole-dope instead; confirm against the paper.
A constituent of the single 1212 composition's charge-reservoir layer, not a dopant in the other compositions.
As Pb -- part of the (In,Pb,Cu)O layer of the 1212 sample.
Occupies the interlayer site between the CuO2 planes of the 1212 composition.
Shares that interlayer site with Ca.

basis: This rejects the seed. 24 of 26 samples are YbCu4.5, which is not simply Cu-deficient YbCu5: it is reported as a cubic AuBe5-type (C15b, F-43m) phase in which the excess Yb-site atoms order, and YbCu4.75Ag0.25 belongs to the same YbAgCu4 AuBe5 family that the taxonomy's own aube5 entry names. The seed's cacu5 is the hexagonal P6/mmm CaCu5 structure of YbCu5 itself, which is present here in exactly one composition and one sample, so it is kept as the alternative rather than as the label. Note that the taxonomy makes this harder than it should be: cacu5 lists YbCu4.5 as its exemplar and Cu-Yb as an example host, and MP supports it only indirectly -- its YbCu5 P6/mmm mp-1607 (hull 0.000, 3 ICSD refs) is the 1:5 compound, and there is no YbCu4.5 entry at all. The call rests on materials knowledge against both, and the papers (high-pressure resistivity and thermopower of the heavy-fermion YbCu4.5) should settle it.

dopant_roles.basis: YbCu4.75Ag0.25 -- Ag on the ordered Cu site, moving the composition towards YbAgCu4, the AuBe5-type valence-fluctuation compound.

basis: LaNi1-xFexO3 across x = 0.4-0.6 is a simple ABO3 perovskite solid solution on the B site -- LaNiO3 is rhombohedral R-3c and LaFeO3 orthorhombic Pnma, both tilt variants of the same prototype. MP's entries for the host are all computed ordered cells (La2FeNiO6 P2_1/c mp-1223335, La4Fe(NiO4)3 P-1, La4Fe3NiO12 P-1, none ICSD-backed), and their rocksalt-like B-site ordering would make this a double perovskite; that is not what a solid solution synthesised at x = 0.4-0.6 gives, so double_perovskite is deliberately not used. Sr on the A site is the other series in the papers (La1-xSrxFeO3).

dopant_roles.basis: La1-xSrxFeO3 -- A-site acceptor, the carrier knob.
B-site substitution in La(M,Fe)O3; the B site is shared by Ni, Fe and the substituents.

basis: K0.87RhO2 and K0.63RhO2 are the layered alkali rhodate: edge-sharing RhO6 sheets with K between them, the NaxCoO2 family with Rh for Co, and x is the compositional variable that sets the Rh valence rather than a dopant level. Neither MP entry for this host is that structure -- K2Rh2O5 P4/mmm mp-867920 and KRhO3 Pm-3m mp-975134 have no ICSD backing and different stoichiometry -- so the references do not cover the compound and the call rests on composition and materials knowledge.

Elemental Mg and the dilute Mg-Zn-RE and Mg-Al casting alloys (Mg97Zn1Gd2, Mg96Zn2Y2) are hcp Mg with substitutional solutes -- MP Mg P6_3/mmc (194) mp-153, 19 ICSD refs -- so the seed holds for those. It does not hold for the Mg2.10(Si0.3Sn0.7)xGay compositions, which are Mg2(Si,Sn) antifluorite thermoelectrics whose formula string has been parsed with the (Si,Sn) group at a few per cent, dropping Si and Sn below the 5 at.% host cut and routing the composition to a bare Mg host. Those belong to antifluorite, and the split is a parsing artefact rather than a real structural mixture, which is worth fixing upstream rather than in stage 2.

dopant_roles.basis: Mg97Zn1Gd2 and Mg96Zn2Y2 -- solute on the hcp Mg lattice; with the rare earth it also forms the long-period stacking-ordered phase these alloys are known for.
As Zn; Gd and Y drive the LPSO/second-phase formation that the thermal-diffusivity paper measures.
The as-cast and as-extruded binary Mg-Al alloys.

Si appears only inside Mg2.10(Si0.3Sn0.7)0.03Ga0.07-type strings, where the bracketed group has been given a small multiplier; the real material is Mg2Si0.3Sn0.7, in which Si is a host element, not a dopant.
As Si -- a host element of a misparsed Mg2(Si,Sn) composition.
In the same misparsed compositions Ga is the real dopant, a hole donor on the Mg site of Mg2(Si,Sn), which is what that paper is about.

basis: AgSbSe2-xTex across the full pseudobinary is the disordered rocksalt ternary -- Ag and Sb share the cation site of a NaCl lattice, as the taxonomy's rocksalt note already says for AgSbTe2 and AgSbSe2 -- and one of the papers is explicitly on the AgSbTe2-AgSbSe2 pseudobinary. The Ag3SbSeTe2 and CuxAg3-xSbSeTe2 compositions are a different case: at Ag:Sb = 3:1 they lie outside the 1:1:2 rocksalt stoichiometry and the paper calls them a two-phase alloy, so those samples are a rocksalt matrix plus a second phase and the host is recorded as mixed. AgSbTe2 itself is known to carry Ag2Te and Sb2Te3 precipitates, so even the 1:1:2 compositions are rarely single-phase. MP offers only AgSbTeSe P4/mmm mp-1229007 at hull 0.470, a computed ordered cell with no ICSD backing, which is not evidence for or against the disordered structure.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) over 21 compositions, median 0.33. AgSbSe2 and AgSbTe2 are both rocksalt, so the axis does not change the prototype; it does change the band structure and is the variable the pseudobinary papers scan.

dopant_roles.basis: CuxAg3-xSbSeTe2 -- Cu replaces Ag on the cation site, though in the two-phase alloys it may partition between the phases rather than sit on one site.

basis: Every composition is a 123 cuprate with substitutions on both cation sites: Y0.38La0.62(Ba,La)2Cu3O7 and (Ca0.1La0.9)(Ba1.65La0.35)Cu3O7.0-7.2 keep the RBa2Cu3O6+d framework of CuO2 planes plus a CuO chain layer. MP's Ba2LaCu3O7 Pmmm (47) mp-622210 with 1 ICSD reference is that structure for the La end member. The oxygen content 7.00-7.20 is the doping variable of the chain layer, and La-for-Ba is the second, deliberately varied knob rather than an impurity.

dopant_roles.basis: (Ca0.1La0.9) on the R site of the 123 structure -- divalent for trivalent, a hole dopant.
Y and La share the R site; Y0.38La0.62 is the deliberate mix, not a trace.

basis: NdBa2Cu3O7 with La on the Ba site is the 123 structure with Nd on the Y site; MP's Ba2NdCu3O7 Pmmm (47) mp-22719 at hull 0.015 with 2 ICSD references is it. The reference ranking is misleading for this host: its ICSD-primary is BaNd2CuO5 P4/mbm with 6 refs, the insulating 'green phase' that appears as an impurity in Nd-123 processing and that no composition here matches. Oxygen 7-delta is the doping variable.

dopant_roles.basis: NdBa2-xLaxCu3O7-delta -- trivalent on the Ba site, the series one paper is built on.
R-site substitution; Pr is the one rare earth that suppresses superconductivity in 123.

basis: Ba8Ga16Si30 and its off-stoichiometric variants are Ba8E46 -- the type-I clathrate, eight guests in the two cage types of a 46-atom Ga/Si framework -- and the papers say clathrate. MP's Ba4Ga3Si20 Pm-3n (223) mp-1214507 at hull 0.005 is the type-I space group for this chemistry, though with no ICSD backing; the other entry, BaGaSi P-6m2, is a different compound. The Ga:Si ratio near 16:30 is the framework electron count, not a dopant level.

dopant_roles.basis: Ba8-xEux -- the guest site inside the cages, not a framework site.
Au replaces Ga/Si in the covalent framework and changes the electron count.

basis: Bi2S3-xSex from x = 0.3 to 2 is the orthorhombic stibnite ribbon structure, not the layered tetradymite: Bi2S3 is Pnma, and even the most Se-rich composition here (S/(S+Se) = 0.33, i.e. Bi2Se2S) is Pnma in MP (Bi2Se2S mp-1227504, hull 0.022) rather than R-3m. Only pure Bi2Se3 would cross into tetradymite and no composition reaches it. The other MP entry, Bi4(SeS)3 Pmc2_1 mp-1227512, is another computed S/Se ordering of the same ribbons; neither is ICSD-backed.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) over 22 compositions, median 0.67. The two chalcogens share the three anion sites of the stibnite ribbon; the prototype is unchanged across the measured range, though the pure-Se end member would be tetradymite.

dopant_roles.basis: CuxBi2SeS2 -- Cu intercalates between the Bi2S3 ribbons and the paper reports nano-scale precipitates, so part of it is a second phase rather than in the lattice.
Added as BiCl3; the halogen sits on the chalcogen site as a donor, the standard n-type route for Bi2S3.
Added as CuI -- halogen donor on the anion site.

basis: SnCCo3 is the metallic antiperovskite exactly as the taxonomy's exemplar states -- C at the octahedral centre of a Co6 octahedron with Sn at the cube corner -- and MP's Co3SnC Pm-3m (221) mp-20679 with 1 ICSD reference matches. All the substituted compositions keep the Co3C framework and vary only the A site.

dopant_roles.basis: Sn1-xSbxCCo3 -- donor on the A site, the main doping series of the chemical-doping paper.
Sn0.95Ag0.05CCo3 -- acceptor on the same site.
The AXD3 antiperovskite series includes A = Ge, Sn, In.
GeCCo3 is the isostructural end member, so Ge on the A site is isovalent alloying.

basis: (Hf,Zr)CoSb1-xSnx is the p-type half-Heusler that every paper here names in its title; Hf and Zr share the 1:1:1 X site and Sn is the acceptor on the Sb site. MP's only entry for the host, HfZr(CoSb)2 R3m (160) mp-1224254, sits at hull 0.660 with no ICSD backing -- a computed rhombohedral Hf/Zr ordering, not the cubic F-43m C1b structure, and it is not evidence against the assignment. Sn sits above the 5 at.% cut in most compositions and so counts as a host element, but it is the doping variable of this system.

solid_solution_axis.note: Hf/(Hf+Zr) over 18 compositions, median 0.50. Same group, same site, identical prototype at both ends; the mixture is there to scatter phonons, and the 50:50 point is where these alloys are usually made.

dopant_roles.basis: Zr0.5Hf0.5CoSb1-xSnx -- the acceptor that makes this system p-type; in the x = 0.01 compositions it falls below the 5 at.% cut but plays the same role.
Zr0.5Hf0.5Co0.9Ir0.1Sb0.99Sn0.01 -- isovalent on the Co site, one of the two papers' subject.
The Rh-substitution paper; same site as Ir.

basis: VCoSb (written both ways in the compositions) is a cubic half-Heusler and the papers say so, one of them calling it the 19-electron VCoSb. MP's VCoSb F-43m (216) mp-4076 at hull 0.005 with 5 ICSD references confirms it; the P6_3/mmc entry at hull 0.521 is not a competitor. The 19-electron count means this compound is normally made V-deficient -- V0.95CoSb and V0.9CoSb here -- and that vacancy level is the carrier knob rather than an impurity.

dopant_roles.basis: V0.98Ti0.02CoSb -- the Ti-doping paper; acceptor on the V site, removing one electron from the 19-electron count.
VCoSb0.98Sn0.02 -- acceptor on the Sb site.

basis: One composition, ScZrCo, from one paper on pressure-induced superconductivity, and I cannot pin the prototype from stoichiometry. An equiatomic 1:1:1 of two early transition metals with Co would normally suggest the cubic MgAgAs half-Heusler, but half-Heuslers almost always carry a main-group Z atom, which this has none of, and the 16-electron count is not the semiconducting 18. The alternatives are just as plausible: a B2/CsCl (Sc,Zr)Co solid solution, since both ScCo and ZrCo are B2, or the ordered full-Heusler Co2ScZr. The reference points at the last of those without supporting it -- MP's only entry for the host is ZrScCo2 Fm-3m mp-1188031 at hull 0.000, which is 1:1:2 and not the measured 1:1:1 composition, and it carries no ICSD backing. Recording a guess would put 25 samples into the wrong shard, so this is parked as crystalline-but-unresolved with the candidates named; the paper's structure section settles it.

Every composition is CuCrS2 within a per cent or two of stoichiometry -- the layered R3m sulfide with Cu between CrS2 sheets -- and the papers name it (layer-antiferromagnet CuCrS2, copper chromium disulfide). MP has it as CrCuS2 R3m (160) mp-5862 at hull 0.039 with 4 ICSD references. The reference ranking disagrees and is wrong here: the host's ICSD-primary is the thiospinel Cr2CuS4 Fd-3m with 16 references, a different compound that appears in none of the compositions. Cu0.9CrS2 and CuCrS2.00-2.10 are Cu deficiency and S excess on the same lattice, which is the ordered-defect behaviour one paper is about.

dopant_roles.basis: Two compositions only; the octahedral Cr site is the likelier host but this needs the paper.

basis: Every composition is CrSb2 with dilute substitutions, and CrSb2 is the orthorhombic marcasite that the taxonomy names alongside FeSb2: MP CrSb2 Pnnm (58) mp-22498 with 9 ICSD references. The host's other 9-reference entry, CrSb P6_3/mmc, is the NiAs-type monoantimonide -- present in the chemistry but in none of these compositions, so the 1:2 stoichiometry decides. The I4/mcm CrSb2 (mp-2666, hull 0.139, 2 refs) is a high-pressure form, not a phase reached on heating within the 10-316 K window measured here.

other_polymorphs.note: CrSb2 I4/mcm, hull 0.139 with 2 ICSD references against 9 for Pnnm.

dopant_roles.basis: Donor on the pnictogen site of CrSb2-xTex.
CrSb1.99Sn0.01 -- the Sn-for-Sb paper; acceptor on the same site.
Cr1-xMnxSb2, the subject of one paper.
RuSb2 is isostructural marcasite, so Ru on the Cr site is isovalent alloying.

basis: (Ge0.5Sn0.5Te)nSb2Te3 for n = 4, 7, 12 and GeSnSb2Te5 are GST homologues with Sn sharing the Ge site, and the first paper calls them layered germanium tin antimony tellurides. But the second paper describes the same series as a nanostructured rocksalt-type solid solution, and both are right: these compositions crystallise as a metastable cation-vacancy rocksalt and order into the layered homologue on annealing, so the host holds both prototypes and needs a per-composition (really per-sample) split. I have deliberately not recorded that as a thermal phase sequence. The taxonomy's transition for gst_homologous -- amorphous to cubic at ~420 K, cubic to layered above ~500 K -- is the crystallisation sequence of a sputtered film; these are bulk ingots that are already crystalline at the start of the measurement, the cubic-to-layered step is an irreversible ordering rather than a reversible transition, and which sample starts cubic cannot be read off the formula. Sn0.57Sb0.13Ge0.3Te is a further case: at 57% Sn it is a rocksalt (Ge,Sn,Sb)Te alloy rather than a homologue. MP offers only computed R3m cells at hull ~0.29 with no ICSD backing.

solid_solution_axis.note: Ge/(Ge+Sn) over 18 compositions, median 0.50. Ge and Sn share the cation site of both the rocksalt blocks and the layered homologue, so the axis does not decide the prototype; the thermal history does.

dopant_roles.basis: Bi2Te3 and Sb2Te3 blocks are interchangeable, so Bi on the Sb site is isovalent alloying.

basis: HfTe5 is 14 of 25 samples and the rest are substituted HfTe5; TEDesignLab gives HfTe5 Cmcm (63) mp-1168 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, which is the prototype itself. The other Hf-Te phases in the references (HfTe2 P-3m1, HfTe3 P2_1/m, Hf3Te2, Hf5Te4) exist in the chemistry but match no composition here. The resistivity anomaly HfTe5 shows near 80 K, inside the measured window, is an electronic/CDW-like crossover rather than a change of prototype, so no phase split is recorded.

dopant_roles.basis: Hf0.95Ti0.05Te5 -- same group, same site; the Ti-substitution paper is about the power factor of the pentatelluride.
Hf0.75Ce0.25Te5 -- note this is 25% of the Hf site even though Ce is only ~4 at.% of the formula, because Te5 dominates the denominator. It is substantial substitution, not dilute doping.
The rare-earth series Hf0.75Ln0.25Te5 all take the Hf site.

basis: 24 of 25 samples are NbSe2 or Cr-doped NbSe2, which is the 2H trigonal-prismatic dichalcogenide the taxonomy's mos2_2h note names explicitly; TEDesignLab gives NbSe2 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1072113 at hull 0.001 with 12 ICSD references. The single NbSe3 sample is the monoclinic chain compound (MP P2_1/m (11) mp-525, hull 0.000, 5 ICSD refs), so both seed hypotheses are real and the host splits on the Se:Nb ratio, 2 against 3. The 33 K charge-density wave and 7 K superconductivity of 2H-NbSe2 fall inside the measured range but are electronic, not changes of prototype.

other_polymorphs.note: NbSe2 P-6m2, the 1H monolayer-like polytype: 1 ICSD reference against 12, and not what a bulk crystal gives.

dopant_roles.basis: Cr0.0009NbSe2 -- extremely dilute. Cr in a layered dichalcogenide normally intercalates into the van der Waals gap, and the paper uses it as controlled disorder to probe the charge order; substitution on the Nb site is the alternative.

basis: SrZrO3, Yb/Gd co-doped SrZr1-xO3-delta and SrZr0.8Co0.2O3 are ABO3 perovskites; the coatings are thermal-barrier zirconates, where the oxygen vacancies created by the trivalent B-site substitution are the point. TEDesignLab supplies the whole octahedral-tilt sequence for this compound with an mp_id each -- Pnma (62) mp-4387, Cmcm (63) mp-3626, I4/mcm (140) mp-5076 and cubic Pm-3m (221) mp-3323, with 6, 2, 10 and 10 ICSD references -- and the measured 299-1674 K window crosses all three tilt transitions of undoped SrZrO3 (roughly 1020 K, 1110 K and 1440 K). Those are recorded as phases because each has its own structure entry for stage 2, but the prototype never changes: this is a distortion series like WO3's, not a change of family. The temperatures are literature values for undoped SrZrO3 and will shift with 10-20% Yb/Gd on the Zr site, so they are marked as model knowledge rather than paper evidence.

dopant_roles.basis: Sr(Zr0.9Yb0.05Gd0.05)O2.95 -- trivalent on the Zr site, compensated by oxygen vacancies; 5-10% of that site despite being under 5 at.% of the formula, and it is what lowers the thermal conductivity of the coating.
Co-doped with Yb on the same site, for the same reason.
SrZr0.85Al0.15O2.925 -- trivalent on the B site with the same vacancy compensation.

basis: ThO2 is the textbook fluorite oxide and MP's ThO2 Fm-3m (225) mp-643 at hull 0.000 with 19 ICSD references, the best-attested entry for the host, says so. Every other composition is ThO2 with a substituent on the cation site; the CaO- and Y-doped ones are oxygen-vacancy electrolytes, which is what the thermoelectric-power-in-electrolytes paper measures.

dopant_roles.basis: Th1-yUyO2 -- UO2 is isostructural fluorite and U4+ matches Th4+, so this is a full solid solution, not doping; the papers treat it as the (Th,U)O2 fuel system.
As U -- PuO2 is the isostructural end member.
(CaO)0.07(ThO2)0.93 -- divalent on a tetravalent site, compensated by oxygen vacancies; the vacancies are what make it an electrolyte.
Th0.9Y0.1O2 -- trivalent acceptor with the same vacancy compensation.

basis: Every composition is (PbTe)x(PbSe)y(PbS)z: all three end members are rocksalt, so the prototype is unambiguous even though the samples are not single-phase. PbTe-PbS has a miscibility gap and these papers are about exactly that -- PbS- and PbSe-rich precipitates in a PbTe matrix scattering phonons -- but precipitate and matrix share the rocksalt structure, so this is recorded as one prototype with the multiphase character noted rather than as a structural mixture. Na is the acceptor. No TEDesignLab or Materials Project entry exists for this four-element host, so nothing external tests it.

solid_solution_axis.note: Se/(Se+Te) over 18 compositions, median 0.67. S shares the same anion site as a third component, which the pairwise axis detector does not show; all three end members are rocksalt, so the axis matters for the miscibility gap and the band structure, not for the prototype.

dopant_roles.basis: Pb0.98Na0.02Te0.8Se0.1S0.1 -- the standard p-type acceptor on the Pb site, and the curator's composition detail says Na-doped.
Isovalent on the Pb site; Cd is used to move the band offset rather than to add carriers.
Donor on the cation site in the bottom-up engineered nanomaterials paper; may also decorate the precipitates.

basis: TiS2-xSex across the whole range is the 1T CdI2-type layered dichalcogenide with octahedral Ti -- both TiS2 and TiSe2 are P-3m1, so the anion mixing does not change the prototype, and one paper's title is literally 'CdI2 structure type as potential thermoelectric materials'. MP's entries (TiSeS P3m1 (156) mp-1216698 at hull 0.000 and Ti3(SeS2)2 P3m1 mp-1217140) are ordered S/Se decorations of that same layer, with the symmetry lowered by the ordering rather than by a different structure; neither is ICSD-backed.

solid_solution_axis.note: S/(S+Se) over 22 compositions, median 0.19. Both end members are 1T, so the prototype holds across the axis; the ratio tunes the band overlap and the lattice thermal conductivity.

dopant_roles.basis: CuxTiS1.5Se0.5 and CuxTiSe2-ySy -- Cu intercalates into the van der Waals gap, which the taxonomy already flags as the doping variable for this prototype rather than an impurity.

basis: Elemental Ag plus dilute fcc alloys at 0.05-4 at.% (Ag98.32Pt1.68, Ag96.85Mn3.85, Ag0.9995Mg0.0005) -- face-centred cubic Cu-type, MP Ag Fm-3m (225) mp-124 with 22 ICSD references. The papers are classic dilute-alloy thermopower work (Kondo-regime AgMn) plus an absolute-Seebeck measurement on a single silver nanowire, which is a form factor, not a different structure. The hcp and R-3m Ag entries in MP (hull 0.003-0.006, 1 ICSD ref between them) are not what a drawn or cast sample gives.

dopant_roles.basis: Ag96.85Mn3.85 -- the dilute magnetic impurity of the AgMn Kondo thermopower paper.
Ag98.07Pt1.93 and similar -- substitutional solute on the fcc lattice.
Ag and Au are completely miscible fcc metals.
Ag0.9995Mg0.0005 -- 500 ppm, a genuinely dilute solute.

basis: ZrB2 is 18 of 24 samples and Zr34B66 is the same 1:2 composition written in atomic per cent; it is the AlB2 C32 type, MP ZrB2 P6/mmm (191) mp-1472 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references. The seed is right for those but does not cover the rest of the host. ZrB12 is the UB12 dodecaboride (MP Fm-3m (225) mp-1084, hull 0.017, 7 ICSD refs) and is the subject of one paper, and Zr6.7B93.3 is ZrB13.9, essentially that phase with excess boron. Zr14B86 (ZrB6.1) and Zr11B89 (ZrB8.1) fall between ZrB2 and ZrB12 where no line compound exists -- MP's ZrB6 Pm-3m sits at hull 0.408, so a CaB6-type hexaboride is not a plausible reading -- and they are most likely two-phase mixtures of a boride with boron-rich framework boron, which the taxonomy's boron_carbide entry covers. So the host needs three labels and a split by B:Zr ratio.
